The regex _PROPOSAL_METADATA_PATTERN (re.DOTALL, non-greedy .*?) terminates at the first '-->' in the document, delivering a truncated JSON fragment to _parse_proposal_metadata, which returns {} on JSONDecodeError. The record's proposal_hash then resolves to None and _recent_proposal_hashes silently skips it, making the proposal invisible to the 24-hour duplicate check.
findings.evidence: tools.py:728-738: metadata_comment = json.dumps({...'signing_key_id': signing_key_id...}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')); '>' not in json.ESCAPE_DCT. tools.py:47: _PROPOSAL_METADATA_PATTERN = re.compile(r'<!--\s*proposal_metadata:\s*(\{.*?\})\s*-->', re.DOTALL). tools.py:574-582: _parse_proposal_metadata returns {} on JSONDecodeError. tools.py:628-638: _recent_proposal_hashes skips records where isinstance(proposal_hash, str) is False. _SIGNING_KEY_LINE_PATTERN does not validate key_id for forbidden characters before returning it.
findings.impact: An operator who writes key_id=scp-->evil into mcp-signing-keys.pub causes all subsequent proposals to have malformed metadata comments. Those proposals become invisible to dedup, allowing unlimited same-body re-submission. The attack requires key ring write access (privileged). caller_id is also embedded in the same json.dumps; in test or embedded-Python contexts caller_id could be influenced more easily, though the MCP surface does not expose it directly.
findings.mitigation: After constructing metadata_comment, apply: metadata_comment = metadata_comment.replace('>', '\u003e'). Alternatively, validate signing_key_id and caller_id for the substring '-->' before embedding and raise ValueError (→ SCP-MCP-E021) if found. Add a test asserting that a signing_key_id containing '-->' either raises SCP-MCP-E021 or produces a metadata comment that round-trips correctly through _parse_proposal_metadata.

findings.claim: C-MIN-01 from R1 is unaddressed. The PROP-NNN slot-allocation while-True loop (tools.py:1162) has no iteration upper bound. Each _proposal_branch_exists call inside the loop carries a 30-second timeout (DEFAULT_GIT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30). With N orphaned git branches (proposals/PROP-NNN branches without corresponding .md files), the loop makes N sequential git show-ref calls holding _PROPOSAL_LOCK for up to 30×N seconds, blocking all concurrent callers.
findings.evidence: tools.py:1162-1174: while True with unconditional next_proposal_number += 1 and no break guard on iteration count. tools.py:38: DEFAULT_GIT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30 used by _proposal_branch_exists:781. _PROPOSAL_SCAN_LIMIT=2048 caps _iter_existing_proposals but not this loop. subprocess.TimeoutExpired from _proposal_branch_exists propagates immediately (tools.py:1169), so one timeout ends the loop early, but only after 30s.
findings.impact: An environment with orphaned branches from SB-MAJ-001 advisory PID-restart cycles can hold the global threading+flock lock for minutes. Under the 32-connection concurrency limit planned for 021H, a burst of concurrent propose() calls queuing behind this lock would hit the 120s per-connection timeout after roughly 4 orphaned branch slots. Liveness degradation, not a direct safety bypass, but amplified by the residual advisory PID restart vector.
findings.mitigation: Add an explicit cap: if next_proposal_number > initial_proposal_number + 1024: return _error('SCP-MCP-E021', 'proposal ID space exhausted after 1024 attempts; remove orphaned proposals/PROP-NNN branches to recover'). Also consider tightening the per-call timeout inside this loop to 5 seconds, since refs/heads lookups are local-repo operations.

findings.claim: SB-MIN-006 from R1 is unaddressed. _stdio_caller_id (tools.py:672-674) falls back to Path.cwd().resolve() when sys.argv is empty or sys.argv[0] is whitespace-only. The U-21-f §13 resolution text states the derivation is 'stdio:<pid>:<resolved argv[0] path>' with no mention of this fallback. Two distinct callers running from the same working directory with empty argv[0] share a caller_id prefix, merging their rate-limit buckets.
findings.evidence: tools.py:672-674: executable_path = Path(sys.argv[0]).resolve() if sys.argv and sys.argv[0].strip() else Path.cwd().resolve(). WP-SCP-021 §13 U-21-f resolution (plan line 250): 'stdio:<pid>:<resolved argv[0] path>' — cwd fallback absent. In embedded-Python contexts (PyPy embeds, test harnesses that clear sys.argv, __main__ modules invoked without arguments) the fallback fires silently.
findings.impact: Rate-limit partitioning breaks for callers sharing a working directory with empty argv[0]. The documented U-21-f contract in §13 is inaccurate, misleading future implementers of 021I's auth model which must build on the caller_id derivation. Advisory-only impact given SB-MAJ-001 Option A posture, but the documentation gap is real.
findings.mitigation: Replace the cwd fallback with sys.executable (always populated in CPython) or the sentinel string 'stdio:<pid>:unknown-executable' accompanied by TOOL_LOGGER.warning. Update the U-21-f §13 resolution text to document the actual fallback and restate the advisory-only caveat.

findings.claim: _remove_orphaned_duplicate_proposals runs before _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded inside _proposal_creation_guard. When an orphaned file is deleted, it no longer contributes to the caller's rolling-hour rate-limit total. A caller at the 10-proposal threshold who holds exactly one same-hash orphan can recover one quota slot by re-submitting that body, allowing an 11th distinct submission in the same hour.
findings.evidence: propose_impl:1115 calls _remove_orphaned_duplicate_proposals; propose_impl:1128 calls _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded. _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded:642-658 counts records by queued_at >= cutoff. After orphan deletion the record is absent; its queued_at no longer accumulates. A caller with 9 successes + 1 same-hash orphan (effective count 10, would be rejected) has count reduced to 9 after orphan removal, permitting the re-submission to succeed.
findings.impact: Negligible: grants at most 1 additional proposal per orphan-recovery cycle. Not compoundable beyond that boundary because the same-hash duplicate check prevents further exploitation after the recovered proposal is written successfully.
findings.mitigation: Accept as known behaviour consistent with the intent of orphan recovery (the original submission was never delivered). Document in §8 risks or 021E slice notes if auditability of quota accounting is required.

findings.claim: FIND-E02 from R1 is unaddressed. No test verifies that propose() accepts a new submission once the 1-hour rolling window has fully elapsed for all prior submissions from that caller.
findings.evidence: test_propose_hardening.py test_propose_rate_limits_the_eleventh_call: submits 10 proposals at T+0..9min, asserts 11th at T+59min is refused. No test advances now to T+61min and asserts the 12th submission succeeds. _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded:643 uses 'queued_at < cutoff' for the break boundary; the > vs >= boundary condition is untested.
findings.impact: A regression widening the window (e.g. timedelta(hours=2)) or using >= on the cutoff boundary would pass all current tests while making the rate limit permanently sticky once a caller reaches the threshold.
findings.mitigation: Add: submit 10 proposals at T+0..9min; assert 11th at T+59min returns SCP-MCP-E020; assert 12th at T+61min (all 10 originals outside the rolling window) returns ProposeResponse.

findings.claim: FIND-E03 from R1 is unaddressed. No test verifies that two distinct caller_ids each receive an independent quota of 10 proposals per hour.
findings.evidence: _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded:648: filters by record.get('caller_id') == caller_id. No test in test_propose.py or test_propose_hardening.py exhausts the limit for caller A and then submits under caller B to confirm independence.
findings.impact: A regression dropping the caller_id filter (making the limit global) would pass all current tests while silently converting per-caller quotas into a single shared quota, breaking multi-tenant deployments.
findings.mitigation: Add: exhaust 10 proposals under caller_id 'stdio:AAA:/x'; then assert a new proposal under 'stdio:BBB:/x' returns ProposeResponse (not SCP-MCP-E020).

findings.claim: The silent-rot banner text at tools.py:747 reads 'WP-SCP-022-proposal-queue adjudication workflow is not yet live' but WP-SCP-021 §4 021E specifies 'WP-SCP-022 adjudication workflow not yet live'. FIND-E01 (R1 MAJ) corrected only the 'land via' word; the divergence in package name suffix and 'is not yet' vs 'not yet' was outside that finding's scope and remains.
findings.evidence: tools.py:747: '> NOTE: WP-SCP-022-proposal-queue adjudication workflow is not yet live;'. WP-SCP-021 §4 021E (plan:94): 'NOTE: WP-SCP-022 adjudication workflow not yet live; proposals queue until adjudication ships.' test_propose_hardening.py:154 asserts the implementation text, not the plan AC text, providing false confidence that the AC contract is honoured.
findings.impact: Semantic meaning is equivalent. Future parsers pattern-matching 'WP-SCP-022 adjudication' (without the -proposal-queue suffix) may miss the banner. Documentation drift between plan AC and implementation.
findings.mitigation: Align tools.py:747 with the plan AC: replace 'WP-SCP-022-proposal-queue adjudication workflow is not yet live' with 'WP-SCP-022 adjudication workflow not yet live'. Update the corresponding test assertion. No functional change.

structured_review.fixpoint_notes: All 6 R1 MAJ verified closed with direct code and test evidence. R1 FIND-E04 (MIN) additionally closed by the new key-ring error tests. SB-nit-007 closed as a side-effect of the SB-MAJ-003 early-exit fix. No new CRIT or MAJ findings from fresh safety-bypass lens. Eight open items remain at MIN or nit: R2-SAF-001 (silent rollback failure, MIN), R2-SAF-002 (HTML comment injection via --> in metadata, MIN — SB-MIN-005 residual), R2-SAF-003 (no loop iteration cap, MIN — C-MIN-01 residual), R2-SAF-004 (CWD fallback undocumented in U-21-f, MIN — SB-MIN-006 residual), R2-SAF-005 (orphan recovery yields +1 rate-limit slot, nit), R2-COV-001 (rolling-window re-enable untested, MIN — FIND-E02 residual), R2-COV-002 (cross-caller independence untested, MIN — FIND-E03 residual), R2-DOC-001 (banner text diverges from plan AC, nit). Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3 fixpoint criteria — no new blockers, all MAJ closed — slice 021E passes R2 review. Remaining MINs are candidates for a targeted fr2 pass or carry-forward to 021I/021J scope.

r1_maj_closures.evidence: _remove_orphaned_duplicate_proposals (tools.py:792-807) scans existing proposals for any whose proposal_hash matches the incoming body hash AND whose git branch does not exist, then calls unlink(missing_ok=True). It is called inside _proposal_creation_guard at propose_impl:1115, before the duplicate check fires. Same-hash SIGKILL orphan is removed transparently. test_propose_recovers_orphaned_duplicate_after_unclean_branch_creation_failure (test_propose.py:120) exercises the full recovery path end-to-end against a real git repo.

_current_signing_key_id (tools.py:677-708) now raises ValueError in all three failure modes: file absent (line 681-683), OSError (line 685-689), no current=true line found (line 705-708). propose_impl:1109-1112 catches ValueError and returns SCP-MCP-E021 with the diagnostic message. The 'unconfigured-signing-key' sentinel string is gone. test_propose_requires_a_configured_signing_key_ring (hardening:186) and test_propose_rejects_when_no_current_signing_key_is_marked (hardening:203) cover the absent-file and no-active-key branches. R1 FIND-E04 (MIN) is also closed by these tests.

mcp-error-codes.md §SCP-MCP-E020 now reads: 'For stdio callers, the hourly limit is advisory because the caller key is pid + executable path; the branch-not-main invariant remains the hard safety boundary across process restarts.' Option A (documentation) applied per R1 mitigation spec and plan intent. Option B (per-executable-path counter file) remains deferred to 021I. The advisory nature is now surfaced at the error-catalog level accessible to callers and downstream tooling.

Same root cause and fix as C-MAJ-02. _current_signing_key_id raises ValueError rather than returning the literal string 'unconfigured-signing-key'. No silent sentinel is written to proposal metadata. All three failure modes produce SCP-MCP-E021. The 021J genesis-entry anchor concern is resolved because no unconfigured sentinel can now reach the log chain.

ProposeRequest: title=Field(min_length=1, max_length=_PROPOSAL_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH) where _PROPOSAL_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH=500 (tools.py:65, 199); body=Field(min_length=1, max_length=_PROPOSAL_BODY_MAX_LENGTH) where _PROPOSAL_BODY_MAX_LENGTH=65536 (tools.py:66, 200). _iter_existing_proposals accepts max_records defaulting to _PROPOSAL_SCAN_LIMIT=2048 (tools.py:64, 585-624). _proposal_rate_limit_exceeded breaks when queued_at < cutoff (tools.py:650), bounding the scan to the rolling window. test_propose_request_rejects_oversized_title_and_body validates Pydantic rejection at 501/65537. test_iter_existing_proposals_caps_scan_volume validates 2048 ceiling.
